crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Satellite Imagery
children.blurb: Satellite imagery as alternative data covers optical, radar, and thermal observations of the Earth's surface collected by public and commercial constellations.

children.name: Card Transaction Data
children.blurb: Card transaction data covers records generated when a consumer pays with a credit or debit card, whether at a physical terminal or online.

children.name: Sensor and Shipping Data
children.blurb: Sensor and shipping data is a category of alternative data built from physical measurements and logistics records.

children.name: Mobile Location Data
children.blurb: Mobile location data covers the movement and presence signals emitted by smartphones and other connected devices, including GPS fixes, cell tower triangulation, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth proximity, and app-level location permissions.

children.name: Web Data Collection
children.blurb: Web data collection in alternative data means gathering publicly available information from websites, forums, job boards, app stores, social media, and regulatory filings to build datasets that supplement traditional financial and economic data.

sections.body: Alternative data means data that does not come from traditional financial statements or official statistics, and it is often collected by satellites, payment systems, sensors, ships, phones, and web crawlers. In artificial intelligence, these feeds are used to build features, detect patterns, and generate signals for forecasting, risk assessment, and research. Satellite imagery can track construction, crops, parking lots, or emissions. Card transaction data can show shifts in spending at aggregate levels. Sensor and shipping data can reveal supply chain movement and industrial activity. Mobile location data can estimate foot traffic, and web data collection can gather prices, job postings, reviews, and other public signals.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of the work are solved, including ingesting large data, cleaning records, aligning timestamps, and training models to predict simple outcomes. Many parts are not solved, including reliable causal inference, privacy and consent, data quality, survivorship bias, and legal compliance. Alternative data is often noisy, sparse, and changes meaning over time, so a model that works on one period may fail on the next. Coverage varies by region and sector, and validation against ground truth is hard. For market-facing work, the site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, which gives a reference point for testing whether an alternative data signal has any relationship to traded assets. Honest limits include signal decay once a feed becomes widely used and the difficulty of separating correlation from causation.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Satellite Imagery covers overhead observation and computer vision for physical assets such as buildings, fields, and industrial sites. Card Transaction Data covers spending panels, merchant-level aggregation, and the problems of sample bias. Sensor and Shipping Data covers telemetry, port calls, container flows, and industrial sensors. Mobile Location Data covers device pings, foot traffic estimates, and the privacy questions that come with them. Web Data Collection covers scraping, APIs, and public web signals such as prices, listings, and reviews. A reader would go to each page for its sources, methods, and limits, and would use them together when a question spans physical activity, consumer demand, and online behavior.
